thread:
marcus: Spike idea — treat the continuous batcher like a small economy: budget slots per epoch + soft tokens that get minted when a tenant behaves. Could be a more nuanced alternative to blanket microbatch fallback.

elena: Explain the token model quickly? sounds novel.

marcus: Each runtime keeps an epoch counter (e.g., 100ms). For each epoch we mint N slot_tokens proportional to GPU throughput. Tenants earn soft_tokens when they have high cache hit rates and low enqueue latency. On pressure, admission consults both slot_tokens and tenant soft_tokens to decide COALESCE vs TINY_WINDOW vs IMMEDIATE.

yusuf: I like that because it biases efficiency to well-behaved tenants. How do we compute "behaved" cheaply?

marcus: Cheap signals only: local kv_hit_ratio EWMA, enqueue_p95 over 1s, and recent batch_fill_ratio. Combine with simple weighted sum; no sampling.

elena: Operationally, do we need cross-host coordination so tenants don't game multi-worker paths?

grace: Start local-first to keep complexity low. If canary shows cross-host divergence, we can add a lightweight aggregator that emits a cluster-circuit flag rather than per-tenant state. That keeps most decisions local and fast.

yusuf: What about streaming requests and sticky affinity? If a session gets soft_tokens, we should pin that decision for the session lifetime or we lose KV cache affinity.

marcus: Exactly. Admission will return sticky_session_id when routing; coalescer tracks sticky mappings with TTL (configurable, default 30s). Sticky wins over fresh admit decisions.

elena: API surface: admit(request, opts?) -> {route: COALESCE|TINY|IMMEDIATE, sticky_id?: string, reason: string}. Keep opts optional for compatibility.

yusuf: Hysteresis and anti-flap? Token economy needs decay rules. Soft_tokens should decay faster than slot_tokens to recover from transients. Also require k consecutive epochs above threshold before revoking tokens.

grace: Metrics to add: batcher.token_issuance.rate, batcher.tenant_soft_tokens, batcher.epoch_slot_consumed, batcher.sticky_misses. Also reason tags for optimize: REASON_KV_MISS, REASON_SLACK_LOW, REASON_BUDGET_EXHAUST.

elena: How does this interact with Optimize recommendations and cost modeling? If a tenant is repeatedly demoted, Optimize can recommend quantization/packing or advise reserved capacity. Add an event stream for persistent demotions.

yusuf: Backwards compatibility: admit() keeps same base signature; new fields optional. Feature gated behind --enable-token-econ and a feature flag in Console. Canary rollout first.

marcus: Test harness: simulate 5 hosts, 1000 tenants, inject a KV miss storm on 10% tenants. Metrics to evaluate: false_demote_rate < 2%, throughput loss < 10% at default slot fraction, tail latency improvement for affected tenants >25%.

grace: Edge cases: what if attackers try to game soft_tokens by sending short warm-up traffic? Mitigate with min_quanta_required per-tenant and require a sustained good window before granting tokens. Also cap tokens per-tenant per-day.

yusuf: Private deploy note: token generation uses only local runtime metrics; nothing exported. Admins must opt-in to cluster aggregator. Document compliance.

elena: Operator tooling: add rdbctl batcher tokens inspect <tenant> and rdbctl batcher set-tenant-minmode <tenant> <mode>. Operator overrides should emit audit events to /audit/batcher/overrides. ops-bot: will post when override happens.

ops-bot: ops-bot: NOTICE: operator override will be audited under /audit/batcher/overrides.

marcus: Implementation plan: 1) prototype token issuer + admit contract (PR), 2) add sticky-id plumbing in coalescer, 3) expose metrics and Console events, 4) canary + sim tuning.

yusuf: If canary shows instability, fallback plan is global circuit-shrink: temporarily reduce tiny budget fraction to force larger batches rather than more tiny windows. That limits cost blowup.

elena: Sounds good. This token-economy approach feels different from previous designs and might preserve throughput for well-behaved tenants while protecting tail. Let's prototype and iterate on real traffic. :thumbsup:
